Listeners.//: One listener per credential class. Printers get their own TLS port carrying the certificate below and reach /p/* only; everything else is served on UserPort as plain HTTP, for a proxy to terminate TLS in front of. Naming these makes Kestrel ignore ASPNETCORE_URLS. See notes/tls-by-default.md.

Certificates.//: The printer-facing certificate authority. Its private key is the most sensitive secret here - custom_cert is exclusive, so this CA is each provisioned printer's entire trust store. See notes/tls-by-default.md.
Certificates.//ContainerNetworks: Ranges that exist only inside this deployment - a container network. Addresses in them are never offered as somewhere a printer could dial. Docker's default is the default here; compose.yaml overrides it with the network it pins. A deployment whose real LAN uses 172.16/12 should empty this list.

XForwarded.//: Which proxy may speak for the client. Empty means the forwarded-headers middleware is not registered at all - see XForwardedOptions. Set KnownNetworks to the proxy's network; compose.yaml does this for the shipped stack.

PrusaConnect.//PrinterTls: One switch for both ends: the tls line written into a printer's ini, and whether the printer listener binds TLS at all. false is for reading the wire or running a rig - every printer token then crosses the network in clear, and startup warns about it.
